sections.content: Use the imperfecto when a memory opens a scene: it describes the setting, repeated actions and feelings that lasted. In a personal memory, this tense answers what life was like before one particular event changes the scene.

items.spanish: Cuando vivía en aquel vecindario, el aroma del pan entraba por el balcón cada mañana y llenaba la cocina en primavera.
items.english: When I lived in that neighbourhood, the scent of bread came in through the balcony and filled the kitchen in spring.

items.spanish: En mi infancia, los adultos se reunían mientras los niños jugaban y mi madre llamaba desde la estufa.
items.english: In my childhood, the adults gathered while the children played and my mother called from the stove.

items.spanish: Teníamos la costumbre de sentarnos fuera, hablábamos con cariño y escuchaba a los mayores cuando terminaban sus tareas.
items.english: We used to sit outside, spoke affectionately, and I listened to the adults when they finished their tasks.

items.spanish: Aunque vivíamos en calles distintas, nos conocíamos y saludaba a los vecinos cuando pasábamos.
items.english: Although we lived on different streets, we knew one another and I greeted the neighbours when we passed.

sections.content: The imperfecto does not say that a repeated habit ended; it lets the listener enter the background of the memory. In later contrasts, cerraron, visitaremos, viviremos, parecía, sentarse, *nos* sentábamos, esperábamos y jugábamos are forms to compare with that background; preparaba and pareciera can also describe a scene.

sections.topic: the imperfect tense for past habits and descriptions
